author: Electricks94
body: #### PR description: This PR introduces `AoSWrapper` as a nested class of the SoA layout. It provides the same utilities as the SoA class, i.e., `View`, `ConstView`, and `Metadata`, making it a suitable template for `PortableCollections`. The `View` of the `AoSWrapper` class comes with a `transpose` function that copies an element at index i from an `SoA::ConstView` to the `AoSWrapper`. This function is used to add a `transpose` function to the `PortableCollections` which copies all data from an SoA layout to an AoS layout. The functionality is also added to transpose from an AoS layout to an SoA layout. The idea of this PR was previously introduced by @leobeltra in [#49072](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/49072). This PR sharpens the implementation by closing misalignments between the SoA View and AoS View and strongly extending the test cases to ensure that both work in the same way. Furthermore, SoA element and View methods are now aligned between the SoA and AoS versions as well, and the AoS ConstView can be used together with the `SoAMultiView` introduced [here](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/51458). The data members of the `AoSWrapper` are also designed in a way that they can easily be serialized by ROOT. This means Eigen objects are not directly part of the `aos_` data member. Instead, Eigen objects are represented by `std::array` on the buffer, and `Eigen::Map` is used for the data access in the View. ROOT I/O and schema evolution are tested by a set of tests used for the SoA version as well Furthermore, the layout of the `TrackingRecHitsSoACollection` is switched from an SoA to an AoS layout. This means that the input to the CA extension uses an AoS data layout with the changes proposed by this PR. The changes have been benchmarked using the following workflow: ``` cmsDriver.py Phase2 -s L1P2GT,HLT:75e33_trackingOnly \ --processName=HLTX \ --conditions auto:phase2_realistic_T35 \ --geometry ExtendedRun4D110 \ --era Phase2C17I13M9 \ --customise SLHCUpgradeSimulations/Configuration/aging.customise_aging_1000 \ --eventcontent FEVTDEBUGHLT \ --filein=$ALL_FILES \ --mc \ --inputCommands="keep *, drop *_hlt*_*_HLT, drop triggerTriggerFilterObjectWithRefs_l1t*_*_HLT" \ -n 1000 \ --procModifiers ngtScouting \ --no_exec \ --output={} \ --python_filename timing_config.py ``` The benchmark was executed as `patatrack-scripts/benchmark --preset hltPhase2 --nvidia-mps -- timing_config.py` on a full node of the NGT cluster using 4 x NVIDIA L40S GPUS and 2 x AMD EPYC 9534 64-Core Processors with 16 jobs, 16 threads, and 16 streams and using NVIDIA MPS active thread percentage: 16 job(s) @ 25%. This PR suggests using an AoS layout for the `TrackingRecHitsSoACollection`, which increases the throughput to `442.1 ev/s` from the default `345.5 ev/s`. This means the workflow can profit from a higher throughput using the AoS layout and running on GPU. Equivalent measurements on CPU only showed no significant difference between the AoS and the SoA data layout in this case. Using nsight compute to profile the kernels shows that most of the improvements reported here come from fewer cache misses in the AoS version. Exemplarily, the memory chart of the [GetDoubletsFromHisto kernel is shown here](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/cecbb6f0b14f31365b23ecf5ec702f4990cad268/RecoTracker/PixelSeeding/plugins/alpaka/CAPixelDoubletsAlgos.h#L169). The reason why the AoS layout achieves better cache utilization here might be too random memory accesses. The total GPU memory consumption of the benchmarks is shown here: It shows slightly higher peaks (about 1GB) for the AoS version. @leobeltra @felicepantaleo FYI
title: Support for AoS datalayout for SoATemplate
